issues.feedback: The `gh issue list --label ralph:ready` then label-swap flow is not truly atomic. The spec needs a compare-and-set style claim protocol (and post-claim verification) to prevent double-claim or stale-claim behavior.

Behavior is undefined when commit+push succeeds but updating issue labels fails. On restart, resetting `in-progress` to `ready` can cause duplicate execution. Define reconciliation that first derives completion from Git and then repairs labels.

You define malformed commits (subject/trailer mismatch) but not the runtime policy. Specify exact handling: fail task label, halt branch, or auto-repair strategy; otherwise resume behavior is ambiguous.
`origin/HEAD` may be unset or invalid in some remotes. Add fallback logic (resolve remote default branch explicitly) and an acceptance test for empty/misconfigured remotes.

Startup reset/checkout rules can discard unrelated local work unless execution is guaranteed in an isolated daemon worktree. The spec should explicitly require isolated worktrees and define dirty-tree preconditions.

Requirement says every transition produces exactly one commit, but some transitions may have no file changes. Specify whether `--allow-empty` is mandatory or which deterministic artifact always changes.
`gh issue list` defaults can miss issues (limit/state filtering). Poll/reconcile logic must define pagination/limits and explicit state filters or task discovery will be incomplete.

Locking by local repo path hash does not prevent two clones of the same remote repo from running concurrently on one host. Lock identity should be based on canonical repository identity (e.g., remote URL + owner/repo).
Lifecycle for `ralph:aborted` and user label edits during execution is underspecified. Define precedence rules (e.g., abort must cancel child and must not be overwritten by exit-status relabeling).

Proposed tests miss key failure cases: push succeeded but label update failed, malformed last commit, no-op commit path, `origin/HEAD` missing, paginated issue sets, stale claim race, and manual abort during in-progress. These should be explicit validate conformance tests.
